AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 15, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDER N-15-21, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE
FROM A REMOTE LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS
DURING A MEETING: YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO:
publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING
THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709
573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER
CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.

  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  RICK RAMIREZ, MAYOR
  ANA VALENCIA, VICE MAYOR
  TONY AYALA, COUNCILMEMBER
  JENNIFER PEREZ, COUNCILMEMBER
  MARGARITA L. RIOS, COUNCILMEMBER
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.
   STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT
  CODE §54956.9(d)(1) City of Norwalk vs. Regional Water Quality Control Board, Case No.
  21STCP04148.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT
  CODE §54956.9(d)(1) City of Norwalk vs. Sami Ammari, Case No. 21STCV31104.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION  PURSUANT  TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE §54956.9(d)(4) in one case.

  IV.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8, Assessor Parcel Numbers 8047-006-924 and 8047-006-925; Negotiating on behalf of the
  City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; Negotiating Party: Primestor; Under Negotiation: Price and
  Terms of Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Ronald Spencer
  Faith Church of Norwalk

FLAG SALUTE
  Matthew Becerra, 8th grade, ASB President
  Lakeside Middle School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize the Distinguished Bus Operator of the Year.

  II.  City Council to recognize the winners of the Holiday Home Décor contest.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS
   1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Department highlight video.

  3.  Week in Review video.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of
  February 1, 2022. 825-04

  Minutes

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period January 9, 2022 –
  January 22, 2022, in the total amount of $951,417.85. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  January 27, 2022 – February 9, 2022 in the total amount of $2,555, 094.19. 640

  Warrant Register

  5.  CLAIM AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Sophia Guzman.
  830-07

  Report

  6.  ORDINANCE 22-1729 – AMENDING NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 13.20.310 OF
  CHAPTER 13.20 RELATING TO THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PIPELINE FRANCHISE FEES - Staff
  recommends City Council accept for second reading and adopt Ordinance No. 22-1729, AN
  ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AMENDING NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION
  13.20.310 OF CHAPTER 13.20 OF TITLE 13 PUBLIC SERVICES. 618-01/860-02

  Report

  7.  AUTHORIZATION TO SUBMIT EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY PROGRAM FOR YEARS
  2022-2025 - Staff recommends City Council authorize the Executive Director of Regional
  Transportation to submit the updated Equal Employment Opportunity Program to Federal
  Transportation Administration by the deadline of March 1, 2022. 1105-01

  Report

  8.  PROJECT NO. 7927 - AWARD ENGINEERING SERVICES AGREEMENT FOR LOCAL STREET
  REHABILITATION PROGRAM – PHASE II, ZONE 3 – Staff recommends City Council award a
  professional services agreement to JMDiaz Inc., in the amount of $367,000 to provide design services
  for Project No. 7927, Local Streets Rehabilitation Program - Phase II, Zone 3 Streets; and authorize
  the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments, provided there is funding in the
  budget and it is within the City Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by
  the City Attorney. 1005-04-7927

  Report

  9.  PROJECT NO. 7928 - AWARD ENGINEERING SERVICES AGREEMENT FOR LOCAL STREET
  REHABILITATION PROGRAM – PHASE II, ZONE 8 – Staff recommends City Council award a
  professional services agreement to Willdan Engineering in the amount of $220,000 to provide design
  services for Project No. 7928, Local Streets Rehabilitation Program - Phase II, Zone 8 Streets; and
   authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments, provided there is funding
  in the budget and it is within the City Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney. 1005-04-7928

  Report

  10. PROJECT NO. 7929 - AWARD ENGINEERING SERVICES AGREEMENT FOR LOCAL STREET
  REHABILITATION PROGRAM – PHASE II, ZONE 19 - Staff recommends City Council award a
  professional services agreement to Onward Engineering in the amount of $340,400 to provide design
  services for Project No. 7929, Local Streets Rehabilitation Program - Phase II, Zone 19 Streets; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments, provided there is funding
  in the budget and it is within the City Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney. 1005-04-7929

  Report

  11. RESOLUTION NO. 22-14 – ESTABLISHING NO MAXIMUM CAMPAIGN CONTRIBUTION LIMITS
  FOR CITY COUNCIL ELECTIONS – Staff seeks City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-14, A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK ESTABLISHING NO LIMIT FOR
  CAMPAIGN CONTRIBUTIONS. 845-05

  Report

  12. MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT FOR A PARATRANSIT USER SIDE SUBSIDY TRANSPORTATION
  PROGRAM – Staff recommends City Council approve the agreement between the Cities of Norwalk
  and Santa Fe Springs to continue participation in the Paratransit User Side Subsidy Transportation
  Program and NTS Route 3 Fixed Route Service Passenger Subsidy Program for term from February
  15, 2022 through June 30, 2027; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney. 1120-07

  Report

  13. ASSEMBLY BILL 361 FINDINGS - Staff recommends City Council make the following findings:

  a.  City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the state of emergency.

  b.  Both of the following circumstances exist (i) The state of emergency continues to directly impact
  the ability of the members to meet safely in person and (ii) City Council continues to impose or
  recommend measures to promote social distancing including remote or hybrid meeting
  participation. 825

  Report

  14. REQUEST FOR USE OF CIVIC CENTER LAWN FOR CARNIVAL – Staff recommends City Council
  approve the carnival requested by the Lions Club of Norwalk for the dates of Thursday, May 26 through
  Monday, May 30, 2022 and waive the security deposit as requested consistent with past practice. 920-
  01-02

  Report

  15. AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 6 FOR BUS STOP CLEANING SERVICES - Staff recommends City
  Council approve Amendment No. 6 to the agreement with Nationwide Environmental Services, a
  division of Joe’s Sweeping Inc. for citywide bus stop cleaning services; and authorize the City Manager
  to execute the amendment, providing there is funding in the budget on behalf of the City, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney. 1120-06

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  16. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report
 PUBLIC HEARING

  17. RESOLUTION NO. 22-13 - NORWALK BICYCLE MASTER PLAN – Staff recommends that the City
  Council adopt Resolution No. 22-13, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK RECOMMENDING ADOPTION OF THE CITY OF NORWALK BICYCLE MASTER PLAN.
  420-06/1005-04-7855 RESOLUTIONS

  Report

REPORTS

  18. RESOLUTION NO. 22-11 – FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW AND REVISIONS;
  AND RESOLUTION NO. 22-12 – UPDATING THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 SALARY SCHEDULE FOR
  CERTAIN GENERAL UNIT EMPLOYEES – Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-
  11, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING
  AMENDMENTS TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 BUDGET; AND RESOLUTION NO. 22-12, A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AMENDING THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2021/22 SALARY SCHEDULE FOR GENERAL AND HOURLY UNIT EMPLOYEES AND
  EXECUTIVE MANAGEMENT AND MID-MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES. 610

  Report

  19. NORWALK  TRANSIT  SYSTEM  PROPOSED  TEMPORARY  FIXED-ROUTE  SERVICE
  ADJUSTMENTS - Staff recommends City Council approve the proposed temporary fixed-route service
  adjustments, effective Sunday, February 20, 2022. 1120-05

  Report

  20. AWARD OF CONTRACT FOR PROJECT NO. 2.126219 – THE HEART OF NORWALK SPECIFIC
  PLAN AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT - Staff recommends City Council award a contract to
  The Arroyo Group for the Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan and Environmental Impact Report in the
  amount of $612,500; and authorize the City Manager to execute the contract and any additional
  amendments not to exceed $673,750, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a
  form approved by the City Attorney. 325-03/1405-06

  Report

  21. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – FEBRUARY EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE –
  Receive and file. 710-07

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated February 11, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
